52b7a1839e.q: What are the five daily practices in Deborah Lovich's Make Work Work book for employee-centric leaders?
52b7a1839e.a: The five practices are: celebrate someone by giving positive feedback in the moment or end of day; leadership through going to where work happens and finding ways to help; be interested by asking people about themselves as humans and remembering details about their lives; co-create by involving impacted employees in changes from the beginning; and do it first by visibly modeling behaviors you ask your team to adopt before requesting it from them.

20fe7e5cdb.q: Why does Deborah Lovich argue employee-centric organizations are seven times more likely to be AI mature?
20fe7e5cdb.a: Lovich published research in Harvard Business Review with Stephen Meyer from Columbia Business School showing that when organizations approach AI with employee-centric thinking rather than fear-based messaging about job loss or demands for more work with fewer resources, employees actually engage with and adopt AI tools. If you introduce AI as purely a productivity play to reduce headcount, it fails because employees will not engage with tools they believe threaten their employment.

ccf92ec4cf.q: What percentage of companies is Deborah Lovich estimating are stuck in a transaction trap between employers and employees?
ccf92ec4cf.a: Based on Lovich's three decades of client experience, she estimates that over 90 percent of companies are stuck in what she calls a transaction trap—an us versus them dynamic that destroys value. Only about 5 to 10 percent of companies truly get employee centricity and actually act on it, with examples including Costco, Trader Joe's, and Delta Airlines.

97d9c083e7.q: How did Delta Airlines demonstrate employee centricity during airline deregulation when prices were dropping?
97d9c083e7.a: When Delta Airlines entered deregulation and faced price pressures, the executives did not fire employees. Instead, executives took salary cuts so they would not be paid more than the highest-paid employee, the pilots. In response, Delta Airlines employees collectively pooled their own money to purchase an aircraft for the company called the Spirit of Delta, demonstrating unprecedented employee commitment.

3cfaeff38e.q: Why did leadership lose the flexible work strategy after COVID-19 if it was working for employee engagement?
3cfaeff38e.a: Leadership never invested in building the capability and muscle of managers to effectively lead distributed teams, so they reverted to co-location as the default method for building culture, connection, development, coaching, and mentorship. However, Lovich argues those practices were not actually better in physical locations either, since teams were already distributed before COVID through conference calls and remote work patterns.
